1:4.sourceText: Ἐχάρην λίαν ὅτι εὕρηκα ἐκ τῶν τέκνων σου περιπατοῦντας ἐν ἀληθείᾳ, καθὼς ἐντολὴν ἐλάβομεν παρὰ τοῦ Πατρός.
1:4.targetText: I was overjoyed to find some of your children walking in the truth, just as the Father has commanded us.

groups.note: Greek I rejoiced greatly is expressed with the single intensified predicate I was overjoyed. The actual rejoicing verb and degree adverb jointly supply this English phrase.

The actual Greek because-I-have-found clause explains the joy; BSB renders that reason as the infinitival to find. The causal complementizer and finding verb retain the whole construction, not an isolated that = to equation.

Greek from/out of the children gives a partitive subset; English expresses the partitive relation as some of. Some is English nominal support for that source partitive, not a separately written Greek some pronoun.

Greek we received a command from the Father is recast as the Father has commanded us. The actual command, receiving predicate, source preposition and Father noun phrase form this small role-reversing clause; the first-person receive subject becomes us rather than a bare receive = us lexical claim.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with your children.
